title: CHM 101 ( UNIZIK ) : PARTICULATE NATURE OF MATTER, SYMBOLS, FORMULA
subject: CHM 101

questions.question: Which particle is the smallest unit of an element that can enter into chemical combination?
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that has the properties of that element and can enter into a chemical combination.

questions.question: Which particle is the smallest unit of a substance that can normally exist alone?
questions.explanation: A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can normally exist alone and still retain the chemical properties of that substance.

questions.question: Which property defines the number of atoms in a molecule of an element?
questions.explanation: The number of atoms in each molecule of an element is called the atomicity of the element.

questions.question: Which group of elements exists as monoatomic molecules?
questions.explanation: All noble gases and metals exist as monoatomic molecules.

questions.question: Which element exists as a diatomic molecule?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen, nitrogen, fluorine, oxygen, iodine, chlorine, and bromine exist as diatomic molecules.

questions.question: A molecule of which element is tetra-atomic?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is known to exist as a tetra-atomic molecule.

questions.question: An ion is an atom or group of atoms that possesses which feature?
questions.explanation: An ion is an atom or group of atoms which possess an electric charge.

questions.question: Which type of ion is formed by the loss of electrons?
questions.explanation: Cations are positively charged ions formed by the loss of electrons.

questions.question: Nonmetals generally form which type of ion?
questions.explanation: Anions are negatively charged ions generally formed by nonmetals through gain of electrons.

questions.question: A group of atoms carrying either a positive or negative charge is called which term?
questions.explanation: A group of atoms that carry either a positive or negative charge are called radicals.

questions.question: The first letter of an element's symbol must be written using which format?
questions.explanation: The first letter of name of the element is used as its symbols and it must be capitalized.

questions.question: When using the first two letters of an element's name, the second letter must be written in which format?
questions.explanation: The first letter must be capitalized while the second alphabet must be in small letter.

questions.question: Which symbol is derived using the first letter and any other letter from the name?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) uses the first letter and another letter from its name.

questions.question: The symbol for Sodium is derived from which Latin name?
questions.explanation: The symbol Na is derived from the Latin name Natrium.

questions.question: The symbol for Iron is derived from which Latin name?
questions.explanation: The symbol Fe is derived from the Latin name Ferrum.

questions.question: Which element is represented by the symbol K?
questions.explanation: The symbol K is derived from the Latin name Kalium for Potassium.

questions.question: Which element is represented by the symbol Ag?
questions.explanation: The symbol Ag is derived from the Latin name Argentum for Silver.

questions.question: Which element is represented by the symbol Pb?
questions.explanation: The symbol Pb is derived from the Latin name Plumbum for Lead.

questions.question: The relative atomic mass of an atom is compared to which standard?
questions.explanation: Chemists use the atom of carbon-12 to estimate the relative atomic masses of atoms and molecules of other elements.

questions.question: The relative molecular mass of a compound is the sum of which values?
questions.explanation: The relative molecular mass of a compound is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in one molecule.

questions.question: The relative molecular mass of a compound is also referred to as which term?
questions.explanation: It can also be referred to as the formula mass.

questions.question: A mole of a substance contains the same number of particles as atoms in exactly how many grams of carbon-12?
questions.explanation: A mole of a substance is the amount that contains the same number of particles as the number of atoms in exactly 12.00 g of carbon-12.

questions.question: The number of atoms in 12 g of carbon-12 is called which constant?
questions.explanation: The number of atoms in 12 g is 6.022 x 10^23 mol^-1, called Avogadro's number.

questions.question: The number of moles is calculated by dividing the number of particles by which constant?
questions.explanation: Number of moles = Number of particles / Avogadro's Number.

questions.question: The molar mass of a substance is the mass of one mole expressed in which unit?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of any substance is the mass of one mole of that substance expressed in grams.

questions.question: The unit for molar mass is expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Its unit is g/mol or g mol^-1.

questions.question: The mass of a substance is calculated by multiplying the number of moles by which value?
questions.explanation: Mass = number of moles x molar mass.

questions.question: Calculating the percentage composition requires the formula of the compound and which data?
questions.explanation: The formula of the compound and the relative atomic mass of the elements present must be known.

questions.question: The percentage by mass of an element represents its reacting mass in which process?
questions.explanation: The percentage by mass of any element represents its reacting mass in forming that compound.

questions.question: The empirical formula of a compound indicates which feature?
questions.explanation: Empirical formula of a compound indicates the simplest ratio of atoms of each element in the compound.

questions.question: The molecular formula of a compound indicates which feature?
questions.explanation: Molecular formula of a compound indicates the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound.

questions.question: For some compounds, the empirical and molecular formulas are identical. Which compound is an example?
questions.explanation: For some compounds both empirical and molecular formula are identical e.g. H2O, CO2, NH3 and CH4.

questions.question: The molecular formula is always a simple multiple of which formula?
questions.explanation: The molecular formula is always a simple multiple of the empirical formula.

questions.question: A pure ionic compound lacks which type of formula?
questions.explanation: A pure ionic compound has no molecular formula as it has no molecules.

questions.question: The formula of a pure ionic compound states the simplest ratio of which entities?
questions.explanation: They state the simplest ratio of ions in the compound.

questions.question: Which law states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of matter states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in the course of a chemical reaction.

questions.question: Who proposed the law of conservation of matter?
questions.explanation: This law was proposed by John Dalton.

questions.question: The law of definite proportion is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: The law of definite proportion is also known as the law of constant composition.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the law of definite proportion?
questions.explanation: This law was proposed by Proust.

questions.question: The law of multiple proportions applies when two elements combine to form how many compounds?
questions.explanation: The law states that if two elements X and Y combine to form more than one compound, then the masses of X which separately combine with a fixed mass of Y must be in simple multiple ratio.

questions.question: The law of reciprocal proportions involves combining with a fixed mass of which entity?
questions.explanation: The law states that the masses of different elements, A, B, C, which combine separately with a fixed mass of another element D, are the same as, or simple multiples of the masses in which A, B, C themselves combine with one another.

questions.question: Which principle states that the first letter and any other letter from the name of the element are used as its symbols?
questions.explanation: The third principle states that the first letter and any other letter from the name of the element are used as its symbols.

questions.question: Where names of several elements begin with the same letter, the Latin names are used. Which principle is this?
questions.explanation: The fourth principle states that where the names of several elements begin with the same letter, the Latin names of the elements are used.

questions.question: A chemical formula is also called which term?
questions.explanation: A chemical formula also called molecular formula is defined as a collection of chemical symbols that is used to show the elements present in any compound.

questions.question: In the formula NH3, the subscript 3 applies to which element?
questions.explanation: A subscript applies to the symbol before it, so the "3" refers to hydrogen (H) only.

questions.question: When writing the formula of a compound containing a metal and a nonmetal, which element's symbol is written first?
questions.explanation: While writing the formula of a compound containing a metal and a nonmetal, the symbol of the metal is written first followed by that of the non-metal.

questions.question: When interchanging valencies, what should be done with the numeral '1'?
questions.explanation: Interchange the valencies of the elements/ions and write as the subscript. Write them close together and ignore '1' (if it's among the obtained valencies).

questions.question: When radical/polyatomic ions are present, they must be written in which format before the subscript is written?
questions.explanation: When radical/polyatomic ions are present, they must be written in brackets, before the subscript is written.

questions.question: In the formula Ca(NO3)2, the numerals outside the parenthesis act as which function?
questions.explanation: When parenthesis are used in formulae of some compounds, such as Ca(NO3)2, the numerals outside the parenthesis are multipliers.

questions.question: The formula Na2SO4 indicates the presence of how many oxygen atoms?
questions.explanation: The formula Na2SO4 tells you that sodium sulphate contains two sodium atoms, one sulfur atom and four oxygen atoms.
